label: v/0/g/n/i input at original position 2-3 after an a/f/z/1/0/c-rich prefix
explanation: Very sparse conjunctive feature (0.05% of steps). About 70% of its mass is in the original phase at t=2-3, where the input is v, 0, g, n or i (v is the strongest) and the preceding tokens come from {a, f, z, 1, 0, c}. Prefixes starting with a (a a z, a f z) give the largest original-phase values. The other ~30% is in the copy phase, mostly when v is fed back (e.g. v a f <DEL> [v] reaches the max), at recall positions 1, 3 and 4. It never fires at t=0-1, on <DEL>, or at original positions 5 and later. The same input tokens after other prefixes rarely fire it, so precision is low: the feature looks like a threshold over a combination of the recent tokens rather than any one clean token rule. The predicate covers only the original-phase part.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=v (+4.28), phase=2 & in_tok=x (+4.23), in_tok=v (+4.13), prev2_tok=f (+4.12), prev_tok=z (+3.74), prev2_tok=a (+3.65). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-1.99), to_go=0 (-1.24), in_first=1 (-0.12).
